subject: Woven's data curation solution
text:
Hey [NAME]​,

We've recently onboarded Woven by Toyota, among hundreds of other global computer vision teams, so thought it'd make sense to reach out to see if we can help you and the team in a similar way.

Woven's Computer Vision team faced challenges with data curation (Voxel51 & internal tools), which lacked the speed & scalability required to efficiently search through their training datasets (capping out at ~1m images).

At Encord, we've built a high-performance architecture to support indexing and searching through billions of data items (using embeddings visualisations, quality metric filters & natural language searches), enabling CV teams to avoid bottlenecks in model development.

Open to learning more?

subject: Cortex launch. Seven agents. One eval problem.
text:
Hi [NAME]

I saw Cortex launched this week. Seven agents in production, drawing
interpretation live. Having worked with a few companies in the construction
AI space I know the constraint that limits how fast that compounds is
whether your team can close the loop between a wrong answer in the field
and a corrected example back in training, without wasting engineering time.

We work with companies like OnsightIQ and Appfolio, running document and
HITL evaluation pipelines at scale. From experience, I know that the
internal tooling that got you to launch stops scaling when agent count and
project volume both rise at the same time. Both companies hit 5x faster
data throughput and went from 2 months to 2 weeks to get a new project
operational.

Do you have 20 minutes next week for a quick conversation about how to
structure that layer so your engineers stay focused on models?

subject: [COMPANY]'s AI Pipeline
text:
[NAME], 

There's a pattern we keep seeing with ML teams at your stage: engineers burning sprint cycles on a pipeline stage that isn't the actual constraint. 

Labeling is usually the first thing to get attention; it's measurable, the team can point to output, and it's easy to staff up. But when we map the pipeline, the real throughput bottleneck is in curation or validation far more often than anyone expects. Model performance doesn't move. Nobody can explain why. 

We built a diagnostic that identifies which stage it actually is for your setup; maps across curation, labeling, QA, and validation, and generates a fix-priority report. 

If that's useful, I'll send it over.
